ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a sinusoidal voltage source, labeled 5π sin(5000t). Above the power source, a 50 Ω resistor and a 1 mH inductor are connected in series in sequence, and the current I is marked as flowing to the right in this series branch. After reaching the middle node, the circuit splits into two parallel branches to the lower common wire: one is a vertical 1 mH inductor; the other first passes through the right-side horizontal 1 mH inductor, then passes through the right-side vertical capacitor C to the lower common wire. Reasoning: It is required that the current I flowing through the 50 Ω resistor be zero, therefore the left-side series branch should not input current into the right-side parallel network. According to the specified method, for the parallel branch after the left-side series 50 Ω and 1 mH, set its input admittance to zero. The angular frequency of the power source is ω = 5000 rad/s. The inductive reactance of each 1 mH inductor is ωL = 5000 × 0.001 = 5 Ω, so the inductor impedance is j5 Ω. The admittance of the vertical 1 mH inductor branch is 1/(j5). The impedance of the right-side LC series branch is j5 + 1/(jωC), and its admittance is 1/(j5 + 1/(jωC)). Set the sum of the admittances of the two branches to zero: 1/(j5) + 1/(j5 + 1/(jωC)) = 0. From this, the right-side branch impedance must be -j5, that is, j5 + 1/(jωC) = -j5. So 1/(jωC) = -j10. Also 1/(jωC) = -j/(ωC), therefore 1/(ωC) = 10, C = 1/(10ω) = 1/(10 × 5000) F = 20 × 10^-6 F = 20 μF.
